     3	This page is the reference for `entire graph init-agents`: what it writes, how
     4	reruns behave, how Claude inheritance is handled, how to verify that a coding
     5	agent loaded the guide, and how to recover from invalid instruction files. The
     6	behavior described here matches the 0.4.0 release target. Run
     7	`entire graph init-agents --help` for the flags in your installed version.
     8	
     9	## What `init-agents` writes
    10	
    11	Activation is per repository. From the repository root:
    12	
    13	```sh
    14	entire graph init-agents --repo .
    15	```
    16	
    17	The command manages three repository paths:
    18	
    19	- `.entire/graph-agent.md`: the complete operating guide for coding agents.
    20	  It is regenerated on every successful run, so manual edits do not survive.
    21	  Its content is identical to `entire graph agent-guide` output.
    22	- `AGENTS.md`: the canonical cross-agent entry point. The command creates the
    23	  file if absent, appends one managed block if no block exists, or replaces the
    24	  existing managed block while preserving other content.
    25	- `CLAUDE.md`: a Claude Code entry point whose managed block is selected from
    26	  the repository's existing instruction-file topology.
    27	
    28	The direct managed block contains a pointer to the generated guide. Its
    29	identifying lines are:
    30	
    31	```markdown
    32	<!-- entire-graph:begin -->
    33	...
    34	@.entire/graph-agent.md
    35	<!-- entire-graph:end -->
    36	```
    37	
    38	A client that resolves `@` imports loads the guide into context. A client that
    39	treats the block as plain text still receives an instruction to read
    40	`.entire/graph-agent.md` before exploring code.
    41	
    42	## Claude inheritance
    43	
    44	`AGENTS.md` always receives the direct guide pointer. The `CLAUDE.md` block
    45	depends on how that file already reaches `AGENTS.md`:
    46	
    47	- If a distinct `CLAUDE.md` contains a live standalone import whose path
    48	  resolves to the root `AGENTS.md`, its managed block contains only this notice:
    49	
    50	  ```markdown
    51	  <!-- entire-graph:begin -->
    52	  <!-- Entire Graph instructions are inherited through AGENTS.md. -->
    53	  <!-- entire-graph:end -->
    54	  ```
    55	
    56	  The user's `AGENTS.md` import remains in place, and the guide is not imported
    57	  directly a second time.
    58	- If that import is absent or cannot be identified safely, `CLAUDE.md` receives
    59	  the direct guide pointer. Removing or adding a live `AGENTS.md` import and
    60	  rerunning `init-agents` switches the managed block accordingly.
    61	- If `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` resolve to the same regular file through a
    62	  symlink or hard link, the shared file receives the direct block once. The
    63	  link topology is preserved.
    64	
    65	Import detection recognizes standalone relative or absolute paths that resolve
    66	to the root `AGENTS.md`. Mentions inside inline code, fenced or indented code,
    67	HTML comments, or the managed block do not count. Ambiguous Markdown keeps the
    68	direct pointer rather than assuming inheritance. `init-agents` does not create
    69	or remove the user-owned `AGENTS.md` import itself.
    70	
    71	## Preflight and rerun behavior
    72	
    73	Before its first write, `init-agents` inspects both instruction paths, reads
    74	each distinct file, validates the marker layout, and renders all managed
    75	content from that validated snapshot.
    76	
    77	Each path must be missing or resolve to a regular file. Symlinks to regular
    78	files are supported, with the target written either relatively or as an
    79	absolute path, as long as it stays inside the project root; a symlink that
    80	resolves outside is refused and nothing is installed. Staying inside the project
    81	root is necessary but not sufficient: a symlink that lands inside a git
    82	directory — `.git` at any depth, including a nested checkout's and a linked
    83	worktree's `.git` pointer — is refused as well. `.git` is inside the project root
    84	but is not project content, and no instruction file belongs there; writing a
    85	managed block into `config` or a hook would corrupt the repository rather than
    86	configure an agent. The git directory is recognised by its structure rather than
    87	by its name, so a repository whose administrative directory is not called `.git`
    88	— `git init --separate-git-dir=admin`, or a checkout driven by `GIT_DIR` — is
    89	covered by the same refusal.
    90	
    91	The landing must also be an agent-instruction file. An alias exists so that
    92	`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` can share one instruction file, so a target that is
    93	markdown by extension, or a rules file such as `.cursorrules`, is written; a

     3	This page is the reference for `entire graph init-agents`: what it writes, how
     4	reruns behave, how Claude inheritance is handled, how to verify that a coding
     5	agent loaded the guide, and how to recover from invalid instruction files. The
     6	behavior described here matches the 0.4.0 release target. Run
     7	`entire graph init-agents --help` for the flags in your installed version.
     8	
     9	## What `init-agents` writes
    10	
    11	Activation is per repository. From the repository root:
    12	
    13	```sh
    14	entire graph init-agents --repo .
    15	```
    16	
    17	The command manages three repository paths:
    18	
    19	- `.entire/graph-agent.md`: the complete operating guide for coding agents.
    20	  It is regenerated on every successful run, so manual edits do not survive.
    21	  Its content is identical to `entire graph agent-guide` output.
    22	- `AGENTS.md`: the canonical cross-agent entry point. The command creates the
    23	  file if absent, appends one managed block if no block exists, or replaces the
    24	  existing managed block while preserving other content.
    25	- `CLAUDE.md`: a Claude Code entry point whose managed block is selected from
    26	  the repository's existing instruction-file topology.
    27	
    28	The direct managed block contains a pointer to the generated guide. Its
    29	identifying lines are:
    30	
    31	```markdown
    32	<!-- entire-graph:begin -->
    33	...
    34	@.entire/graph-agent.md
    35	<!-- entire-graph:end -->
    36	```
    37	
    38	A client that resolves `@` imports loads the guide into context. A client that
    39	treats the block as plain text still receives an instruction to read
    40	`.entire/graph-agent.md` before exploring code.
    41	
    42	## Claude inheritance
    43	
    44	`AGENTS.md` always receives the direct guide pointer. The `CLAUDE.md` block
    45	depends on how that file already reaches `AGENTS.md`:
    46	
    47	- If a distinct `CLAUDE.md` contains a live standalone import whose path
    48	  resolves to the root `AGENTS.md`, its managed block contains only this notice:
    49	
    50	  ```markdown
    51	  <!-- entire-graph:begin -->
    52	  <!-- Entire Graph instructions are inherited through AGENTS.md. -->
    53	  <!-- entire-graph:end -->
    54	  ```
    55	
    56	  The user's `AGENTS.md` import remains in place, and the guide is not imported
    57	  directly a second time.
    58	- If that import is absent or cannot be identified safely, `CLAUDE.md` receives
    59	  the direct guide pointer. Removing or adding a live `AGENTS.md` import and
    60	  rerunning `init-agents` switches the managed block accordingly.
    61	- If `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` resolve to the same regular file through a
    62	  symlink or hard link, the shared file receives the direct block once. The
    63	  link topology is preserved.
    64	
    65	Import detection recognizes standalone relative or absolute paths that resolve
    66	to the root `AGENTS.md`. Mentions inside inline code, fenced or indented code,
    67	HTML comments, or the managed block do not count. Ambiguous Markdown keeps the
    68	direct pointer rather than assuming inheritance. `init-agents` does not create
    69	or remove the user-owned `AGENTS.md` import itself.
    70	
    71	## Preflight and rerun behavior
    72	
    73	Before its first write, `init-agents` inspects both instruction paths, reads
    74	each distinct file, validates the marker layout, and renders all managed
    75	content from that validated snapshot.
    76	
    77	Each path must be missing or resolve to a regular file. Symlinks to regular
    78	files are supported, with the target written either relatively or as an
    79	absolute path, as long as it stays inside the project root; a symlink that
    80	resolves outside is refused and nothing is installed. Staying inside the project
    81	root is necessary but not sufficient: a symlink that lands inside a git
    82	directory — `.git` at any depth, including a nested checkout's and a linked
    83	worktree's `.git` pointer — is refused as well. `.git` is inside the project root
    84	but is not project content, and no instruction file belongs there; writing a
    85	managed block into `config` or a hook would corrupt the repository rather than
    86	configure an agent. The git directory is recognised by its structure rather than
    87	by its name, so a repository whose administrative directory is not called `.git`
    88	— `git init --separate-git-dir=admin`, or a checkout driven by `GIT_DIR` — is
    89	covered by the same refusal.
    90	
    91	The landing must also be an agent-instruction file. An alias exists so that
    92	`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` can share one instruction file, so a target that is
    93	markdown by extension, or a rules file such as `.cursorrules`, is written; a
    94	target that is some other existing file — a `Makefile`, `.envrc`, or
    95	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — is refused rather than having a managed block
    96	appended to it. A target that does not exist yet is still created, which is what
    97	the dangling-alias case below relies on, and a target this command wrote on an

   109	### Credential-store path exclusions
   110	
   111	A built-in exclude list keeps credential stores out of the provider's
   112	working-tree and committed-tree source corpora. Within those corpora, unless a
   113	caller deliberately re-admits one, a denied path is not parsed as source,
   114	indexed, written to graph/search caches, returned in graph or search results, or
   115	quoted in search context blocks.
   116	
   117	This is a corpus and output boundary, not a promise that no local process reads
   118	the underlying file or Git blob. Git-backed search acceleration can scan
   119	tracked or committed blobs before credential-store path rules are applied to
   120	its matches; denied matches are discarded before Entire Graph's content reader,
   121	source parser, caches or responses. The `diff`, `analyze`, `commit` and
   122	`checkpoint` families analyze requested Git ranges rather than the graph/search
   123	corpus, so they can read credential-store paths and report content-derived
   124	metadata about them. Those built-in operations remain local under the provider's
   125	no-egress contract. `verify` runs caller-supplied commands with the caller's
   126	privileges and is outside this exclusion boundary.
   127	
   128	The list covers `.env` and its `.env.<environment>` variants, `.envrc`,
   129	`.npmrc`, `.netrc`/`_netrc`, `.pgpass`, `.htpasswd`, `.pypirc`, `.dockercfg`,
   130	`.boto`, `.git-credentials`, Docker's `.docker/config.json`, Kubernetes'
   131	`.kube/config`, Terraform's `credentials.tfrc.json`, Google Cloud's
   132	`application_default_credentials.json`, SSH private keys (`id_rsa`, `id_dsa`,
   133	`id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519`),
   134	`credentials`/`credentials.{json,yml,yaml,ini,toml}`,
   135	`secrets.{json,yml,yaml,ini,toml}`, key material and encrypted stores by suffix
   136	(`.pem`, `.key`, `.pfx`, `.p12`, `.pkcs12`, `.jks`, `.keystore`, `.truststore`,
   137	`.ppk`, `.kdbx`, `.asc`, `.gpg`), and files ending in `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`,
   138	`.ini`, `.toml`, `.cfg`, `.conf`, `.properties`, `.txt` or `.enc` under a
   139	directory segment named `secrets/` or `credentials/` at any depth. Matching is
   140	case-insensitive. The Git, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and Google Cloud
   141	entries match at any depth and are file-only, so a same-named directory and its
   142	descendants remain searchable.
   143	
   144	Outside those file-only entries, matching retains Git-style path semantics. A
   145	basename or suffix pattern can therefore match a directory segment; when it
   146	does, that directory's descendants are excluded. For example, `*.key` also
   147	excludes `pkg/client.key/**`. This behavior is intentional.
   148	
   149	Classification is based on PATHS, not content: Entire Graph does not inspect a
   150	file's bytes to decide whether an otherwise-unrecognized path contains a
   151	secret. A credential store whose path gives no signal — `deploy/prod-values.yaml`
   152	holding an inline API key — is not covered. Public halves (`.crt`, `.cer`,
   153	`.pub`) are deliberately not excluded, and source code under
   154	`internal/secrets/` or `pkg/credentials/` stays fully searchable.
   155	
   156	The list is loaded after the repository's own exclude files, so a negation
   157	inside the repository under analysis cannot switch it off, and before the
   158	caller's `--ignore-file`/`--include-file`, so `--include-file` remains the way
   159	to deliberately re-admit a path (a checked-in `.env.example` used as
   160	configuration documentation, for example).
   161	
   162	Because of that position the list only ever adds exclusions: it contains no
   163	negation, so it cannot re-admit anything the repository itself excluded. The
   164	bare `credentials` entry — the AWS CLI shape, `.aws/credentials` — is matched as
   165	a FILENAME only for that reason: a directory named `credentials/` is neither
   166	excluded by it nor re-admitted when the repository's own `.gitignore` or
   167	`.graphignore` excludes it.
   168	
   169	Both persistent caches (`index`/`search` snapshots and the streamed record
   170	caches) key on a digest of the effective built-in rules, so a cache entry warmed
   171	by a build with a different policy is not reachable — an entry written before
   172	these rules existed misses instead of re-emitting the paths it named.
